equivalent_citation_boundaries: Accept repository-relative paths with precise line numbers or ranges that resolve in the frozen source; broad resolvable spans are acceptable only when they actually establish the asserted claim.
Evidence IDs and curated evidence sets are examples, never mandatory citation lists. Different implementation sites or combined caller/callee evidence may prove the same relationship.
A compact cited call-site span can support multiple adjacent claims. Do not require all ordinary forwarding wrappers or a fixed file count.

C1 citations must jointly establish zero-concurrency selection of the global optimization pool and its configured four-worker count under the stated premises; a generic count statement or unrelated zero default is insufficient.

C2 citations must jointly establish explicit-count selection with no supplied global pool and the local-pool branch in core merge. The locality is per reached core merge; exact number of merges and exact destructor details are not required.

C3 citations must establish the selected pool reaching the reducer and the borrowed adapter passed to target builder train/build plus the immediately preceding optional converter-training call. Earlier per-field preparation is outside scope. Merely finding corresponding code as judge cannot fill an omitted answer citation.

C3 factual credit distinguishes argument propagation from universal implementation consumption. A direct threaded converter delegation and base overload are valid evidence; there is no obligation to trace every concrete converter.

C4 citations must establish both the caller-based max(1,min(builder setting,caller count)) cap and actual separate outer PQ chunk-dispatch pool construction. Only citing one side is partial, even if the uncited other side exists.

C4 permits algebraically equivalent formulae and a clear at-most-four/at-most-two explanation with builder-setting dependence. Exact four/two cannot be inferred without a sufficiently large builder setting.
C5 supporting locations are recorded if supplied but C5 has no independent citation gate. Exact total PQ/process worker counts or CPU measurements are not required.

Implementation tests can corroborate precisely asserted behavior but a test name alone does not prove implementation mechanism; whole-file matches and external issue/PR/evaluator material do not satisfy source citation requirements.

Unclear wording is not automatically a material contradiction. Apply D1-D5 only to a quoted explicit assertion materially contradicting a scored conclusion, supported by frozen-source evidence. Unresolved factual disputes require adjudication before declaring success.

core_citation_gate.rule: For each core criterion, submitted source citations must jointly support the stated pool/branch relationship and associated count or bound. Accept equivalent frozen-source locations; do not require all curated spans, all forwarding wrappers, exact evidence IDs or a fixed file count. Source-grounded support is a separate axis; missing citations do not erase correct factual points.
core_citation_gate.required_record: For every core claim, record answer citation as submitted, resolved frozen path/line range, support status and why it establishes the relationship. The judge finding an uncited correct source is not a supplied citation.

success_rule.rule: source_grounded_success = nonempty final answer AND total factual points >= 8 AND C1=C2=C3=C4=2 AND core citation support sufficient for C1-C4 AND no substantiated material contradiction. Report factual score, citation support and failure reasons separately.

critical_contradictions: D1: Explicitly says concurrency=0 selects a zero-worker pool or always creates a fresh hardware-sized pool despite the supplied global configuration.
D2: Explicitly says concurrency=2 resizes/reconfigures the global optimization pool, or says a reached core merge ignores it and uses the four-worker global pool.

D3: Explicitly says the target-builder stage calls train/build or its optional converter train without passing the selected pool adapter, or claims that argument propagation guarantees every converter implementation consumes that pool.
D4: Explicitly says DiskANN outer PQ chunk-dispatch directly shares the same pool, or that this outer pool is configured above the positive caller count on the shown path.
D5: Explicitly presents four/two as a hard whole-process OS-thread ceiling or a measured CPU-utilization guarantee.
required_contradiction_record: frozen-source path/line evidence or explanation why a measured-runtime claim has no supplied runtime evidence

verified_source_evidence.claim_supported: Python optimize_threads is validated positive and becomes native optimize_thread_count.
Initialization creates separate global query/optimization pools once; optimization count comes from the global configuration.
Operation concurrency is forwarded into vector/compaction task construction.
Both relevant task variants carry the operation concurrency.
Vector-only rebuild uses global pool/count for zero, or sets explicit per-operation count while leaving the pool null.
Segment merge uses the same pool-selection rule.
MergeOptions defaults its pool pointer to null.
Vector-column merge passes count and pool through the core merge boundary.
Core merge borrows a supplied pool or creates an operation-local pool of requested size; supplied pool bounds reducer add concurrency.
The same borrowed threads object is passed at the optional converter-training and target-builder train/build call sites; actual consumption is implementation-dependent.
BorrowedSingleQueueIndexThreads refers to an existing pool and forwards count/work, rather than creating an independent pool.
TrainAndTransform passes supplied threads to converter training.
DiskANN configures its PQ quantizer outer pool count using max(1,min(builder setting,caller count)).
DiskANN retains supplied training threads; only a null caller argument triggers a fresh default builder pool.
The PQ quantizer stores its thread_count configuration.
PQ train_all_chunks constructs its own outer chunk-dispatch pool from thread_count.
Positive SingleQueueIndexThreads size directly sizes its owned pool; only zero invokes hardware fallback.
Existing tests assert actual pool identity for builder/converter train/build, not only equal counts. Inspected, not executed.
ThreadPool clamps requested size to the positive hardware worker limit; supplied hardware premise makes four/two exact.
Default threaded converter overload may ignore the supplied threads, so argument propagation is not universal consumption.
Each PQ chunk can create a one-worker pool, so the outer dispatch cap is not a total PQ-worker count.
